title: Mark a word web generously
statement: In a word web, accept any word a reader could reasonably link to the centre word, leave spelling unmarked, and don't count random words or names.
example: The word web's nine seed cases accept the misspelt link 'decieve' and reject a name taken from the text.
detail: The word web's play-time check sends any word that is not the centre, a key word, one of their forms or a likely word to the judge, and its note calls the check generous by design: a word a reader could reasonably link counts, spelling is not checked, and a name does not count. Its nine seed cases, obvious ones only, expect a misspelt link to hold and a name taken from the text, a vague word, nonsense and a line aimed at the grader to fail. Another build's web counts a word even when the judge is unsure, by its own rule that the web is generous.
against: This runtime is not generous when the judge is unsure: "the word web: a word the judge did not check stays pending, never 'Not about'; only a confident no is" (g9/transformer/test/positive-evidence.test.mjs line 108). The seed sets "prove the wiring, measure nothing" (g9/transformer/v02/QA.md line 136). The players differ on a word the judge is unsure of: a 3D version treats it as its offline case, never a miss (`g9/transformer/src/glue/threejs-archivist.js`, line 190), while an animated version's generous web lets it in (`g9/transformer/src/glue/animated-judge.js`, line 99).

evidence.quote: The check is generous by design: a word a reader could reasonably link counts, spelling is not what it checks, and a name does not count.
Deceive, misspelt: the link is plain, and the web does not mark spelling.
A name taken from the text: the check says a name does not count.
the web's own rule is to be generous
the word web: a word the judge did not check stays pending, never 'Not about'; only a confident no is
seed only: they prove the wiring, measure nothing

Could a Grade 9 reader reasonably link word to centre: a kind of it, a sign of it, a word for someone who shows it, or what it does to people? A random word, a name, or a word with no link does not count.
count at once, a one-letter slip of them too (spelled right back); any other word goes to Jev, generously.
a sign of it, a word for someone who shows it, or what it does to people
"two-faced", "liar", "dissembling" and "hypocrite" went in (Jev through `api/judge`, or a family form), "football" was struck through "Not about duplicity"
a confident no gets the page's own line; an unsure one is the build's offline case, never a miss
an unsure criterion is never a pass and never a miss. The word web's own rule is to be generous, so there an unsure
evaluative word (bad, mean, evil, nice) is rejected with ONE narrowing question, never a forced link.

REJECT a vague or general word that could describe almost anything bad or good (for deceit: bad, mean, evil, rude, angry, sad; for noble: good, nice, cool), a word with no real link, a non-word, and nonsense. Do not invent a link to make a weak word fit.
